seed: FR-013 classifies empty stdout as an automatic failed call. Does stdout consisting only of whitespace or newlines count as 'empty' and skip extraction, or does it proceed to FR-026/FR-027 extraction and fail there instead?

turns.question: By what criterion in the text would one recognize or verify "FR-013 classifies empty stdout as an automatic failed call. Does stdout consisting only of whitespace or newlines count as 'empty' and skip extraction, or does it proceed to FR-026/FR-027 extraction and fail there instead?"? Cite the lines that establish the criterion.
turns.answer: The text does not establish this criterion. FR-013 (line 152) states only that a model call producing 'empty stdout' is classified as a failed call on the parse-failure path before any extraction, but it never defines what counts as 'empty' for stdout. Elsewhere the spec does define 'empty' explicitly and narrowly for a different object — FR-005 (line 131) defines an empty specification as one containing '0 non-whitespace characters' — but no analogous definition is given for stdout in FR-013, FR-026, or FR-027. Whether whitespace/newline-only stdout is treated as 'empty' (short-circuiting to the failed-call path) or as non-empty content that proceeds to FR-026/FR-027 extraction (and fails there for yielding 0 JSON objects) is left unstated.
